question.leadin: Answer the following about Mesopotamian empires and emperors.
question.text: This ruler of the Babylonian Empire consolidated his power and defeated Rim-Sin of Lagash. His namesake law code included the ruling "an eye for an eye".
question.clue: This Amorite king went up a mountain to receive a stele from the sun god Shamash that was later discovered in Susa.

swap.leadin: Elamite and Akkadian are among the languages that were written in this system despite not being native languages of the civilization that invented it.
swap.text: Name this writing system, developed by the Sumerians, that uses a reed stylus to make wedge-shaped impressions on clay tablets.
swap.clue: Henry Rawlinson studied the Behistun Inscription for insight into this system, which is seen on the oldest complaint tablet.

question.leadin: Identify some civilizations of ancient Mesopotamia.
question.text: One of this civilization's rulers, Ashurbanipal, constructed a large library at its capital of Nineveh. Other rulers of this empire included Tiglath-Pileser and Sennacherib.
question.clue: Accounts of invasions by this empire written by king Taharqa record that its armies had their bowstrings eaten by field mice.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Mesopotamia's earliest civilization, Sumer.
swap.text: Before its ultimate collapse, Sumer experienced a renaissance during the Third Dynasty of this city, which saw the writing of the Epic of Gilgamesh. This city was home to the Great Ziggurat.
swap.clue: A king named -Nammu, who founded a dynasty that supplanted Lagash and the Gutians, was succeeded by Shulgi.

question.leadin: The language spoken in this empire replaced the Sumerian language and is believed to be the earliest Semitic language.
question.text: This Mesopotamian empire was the largest in recorded history at the time. It reached its greatest extent under the rule of Naram-Sin.
question.clue: Its most famous ruler's life was detailed on the Ebla tablets, and started out as a cup-bearer to Ur-Zababa of Kish.

swap.text: The Sumerian king list states this figure ruled between king Dumuzid and his own son Ur-Nungal. In an ancient story, this figure loses his friend Enkidu and learns the secret of immortality.
swap.clue: The British ambassador to Tewodros was Hormuzd Rassam, an Assyrian archaeologist who discovered the clay tablets containing this work about a king of Uruk, the oldest known piece of literature.

question.leadin: This civilization's Ubaid period is said to have been developed from the Samarra culture.
question.text: Identify this civilization whose last king was Lugal-Zage-Si and whose Jemdat Nasr period followed its Uruk period. It developed cuneiform.
question.clue: A tomb built by this culture contains several ornate lyres, as well as dozens of handmaidens who were sacrificed and buried in a "Death Pit."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about ancient rulers who name cylinders.
swap.text: A cylinder discovered in Borsippa named for the Seleucid King Antiochus I Soter was written in the traditional form of this language. The Epic of Gilgamesh was written in this language.
swap.clue: This native language of the Assyrian and Babylonian empires. It was spoken in a namesake empire founded by Sargon over four thousand years ago.

question.leadin: The expansion of the culture based in this city can be traced through its distinctive beveled-rim bowl, and it contained temples devoted to Anu and Inanna.
question.text: Identify this city, whose probably legendary rulers included Lugalbanda and his semi-divine son, Gilgamesh.
question.clue: The Ubaid period preceded this city's namesake "Protoliterate" period.

swap.text: Fragments of Hammurabi's Code have been found in this city, whose "scribal corner" is rich with ancient texts. Various Mesopotamian dynasties sought to control this city of religious importance, the home of the god Enlil.
swap.clue: The best example of a Sumerian schoolhouse was found in this city, which was the center of worship for Enlil. This city's Ekur Temple was rebuilt by Naram-Sin.

question.leadin: The oldest surviving hymn in the world was written in the language of this civilization.
question.text: Name this Hurrian kingdom and rival of the Hittites governed from Wassukani. Its king Tusratta wrote a letter to Akhenaten about "The Missing Gold Statues Again."
question.clue: Based on terms in the Kikkuli horse-training manual, the names of several rulers, and a list of deities found in a treaty, the rulers of this polity are argued to have been Indo-Europeans.

swap.leadin: According to Herodotus, the prayers of the Pharaoh Sethos were answered when field mice destroyed the shields and bows of this man's army.
swap.text: Name this son of Sargon II and father of Esarhaddon who returned to Nineveh after a plague inhibited his attempt to take Jerusalem from the Judean King Hezekiah.
swap.clue: Though he compelled tribute, this ruler was prevented by a plague from capturing Jerusalem from Hezekiah.

question.leadin: In Women of Babylon, Zainab Bahrani argues that Mesopotamian votive statues acted as portraits by referencing an alabaster disc depicting this ruler's daughter overseeing the pouring of a libation.
question.text: Name this ruler, whose daughter Enheduanna was both a poet and high priestess to the god Nanna. This former cupbearer to Ur-Zababa of Kish was raised by the gardener Akki, who had found him floating in a river.
question.clue: After taking Kish from Lugulzaggesi, he built his empire by extending trade from his capital city throughout to Susa and the Zagros mountains.

swap.text: This Sumerian city, which the ancients considered the world's oldest, contained Enki's cult center, the E-Abzu or "House of Deep Waters." Silt accumulated in the Persian Gulf south of this city, where Amar-Sin built a ziggurat.
swap.answerHtml: Eridu [or Irîtu; accept Tell Abu Shahrain; accept Eridu Genesis] (Eridu was once located on the sea, but the silt eventually shifted it over 100 miles inland.)
swap.clue: This Mesopotamian city whose rulers are the first kings mentioned on the Sumerian King List, which is often taken as evidence for this city being the oldest in Sumerian civilization.

question.leadin: While touring a dig site led by this man, Agatha Christie met her second husband, his assistant Max Mallowan.
question.text: Name this British archaeologist who inspired Christie's novel Murder in Mesopotamia by discovering a Royal Cemetery. He also uncovered the Standard of Ur during his 1922-1934 excavation of the city.
question.clue: This archaeologist worked with T. E. Lawrence at Carchemish before leading the 1920's excavation of Ur.

swap.text: Most Sumerian dynasties after the collapse of Akkad came from this foreign group, who invaded Mesopotamia from the northern Zagros Mountains. The victory inscriptions of Ur-Nammu revels in the overthrow of many rulers from these people, whom the Sumerians and Babylonians regarded as barbarians.
swap.clue: "The Curse of Akkad" tells of how Naram-Sin angered Enlil, causing him to summon this people to wreak havoc in his lands. This people from the Zagros Mountains conquered Akkad in the late 3rd millennium BCE.

question.leadin: It was constructed under the order of King Nebuchadnezzar II, and contains many bas reliefs of dragons and aurochs.
question.text: Name this large blue and gold structure located in Babylon. The walls lining the street leading up to this structure were decorated with a brick mosaic of lions and flowers.
question.clue: This gate that was once built into the wall that surrounded Babylon. It is named for a deity.

swap.text: The Great Ziggurat was finished by this king of the Third Dynasty of Ur, the son of Ur-Nammu. This king built a 150-mile wall to keep out the Amorites and claimed to have run from Ur to Nippur and back, a total of 200 miles, in a single day.
swap.clue: This king of Ur, the son of Ur-Nammu, completed the construction of Ur's Great Ziggurat. Misinterpretation of the Sumerian writing system led this ruler's name to be originally read as "Dungi."

question.leadin: This activity often took place in an ambassu with many spectators viewing it.
question.text: Name this activity in which Assyrian rulers symbolically recreated one of Ninurta's deeds. A series of reliefs of this activity shows wine being poured onto the heads of some of its participants.
question.answerHtml: lion hunting [accept Panthera leo persica in place of “lion”; prompt on hunting; prompt on bird hunting or eagle hunting by asking “with what other animal is the Anzû bird commonly associated?”]

swap.leadin: He appeared under the name "Pul" in the Book of Kings. FTPE.
swap.text: Taking the name of a preceding ruler from the 11th Century B.C., this 8th Century ruler and father of Shalmaneser V brought on a new golden age for the Assyrians, conquering Babylon and Syria, and introducing many reforms centralizing the administration of the empire.
swap.clue: This ruler's major campaigns included the subjection of Urartu in 735 B.C.E., and the capture of Damascus during the rebellion of Rakhianu.
